title: Analysis of Topographic Amplification Effects on Canyon Sites Using 3D Boundary Element Method
venue: Journal of Seismology and Earthquake Engineering (JSEE), 9(1), 63-72
methods: parametric study of model, wave and material parameters
key_findings: Canyon length matters more than free-field length for accuracy, and the paper proposes modelling rules for 3D BEM wave scattering. The effect of canyon shape and depth on amplification depends on frequency. Deep (semi-circular) canyons amplify more than shallow (semi-elliptical) ones.
belongs_reason: Consensus lists R. Tarinejad. A web search gives the authors Tarinejad, Ahmadi and Khaji, which fits his Tarbiat Modares PhD period ('Seismic Loading for Canyon Site Structures').

title: Seismic Wave Scattering Analysis using a 3D Boundary Element Method on Topographic Irregularities
methods: parametric study (free-field/canyon length, frequency, incidence direction, damping, Poisson ratio)
key_findings: Free-field length matters little compared with canyon length. Damping, incidence angle and frequency strongly affect scattering, and damped systems show larger displacements on the canyon side facing the incoming wave. Wave parameters change the displacement pattern, while material properties do not.
belongs_reason: Consensus lists R. Tarinejad et al. The content repeats his 2007 JSEE 3D-BEM canyon work. The venue (likely a conference paper) and co-authors could not be verified.

title: Response of an arch dam to non-uniform excitation generated by a seismic wave scattering model
methods: generation of non-uniform ground motion from a single site record
comparison with recorded responses (2008 Chino Hills earthquake, Pacoima Dam)
key_findings: Computed displacements under the generated non-uniform excitation agree well with recorded dam responses. Uniform excitation underestimates displacements. Non-uniform input strongly increases stresses near the foundation and changes the stress pattern: maximum stresses move from the crown cantilever near the crest (uniform input) to the sides and the foundation (non-uniform input).
stated_limitations_or_future_work: Implied: a linear substructure analysis (EACD-3D-2008) validated against a single earthquake (Chino Hills 2008) at a single dam.
belongs_reason: Consensus lists R. Tarinejad as first author. A web search confirms the author list Tarinejad, Fatehi and Harichandran, which matches the known collaborator R.S. Harichandran. The topic (arch dam, wave scattering) is his core line. The DOI comes from a web-search summary of the ScienceDirect page; the page itself could not be fetched.

title: Modal identification of structures by a novel approach based on FDD-wavelet method
structure_type: generic (numerical MDOF systems with regular and irregular mass/stiffness)
methods: modified Morlet wavelet with two free parameters
key_findings: Hybrid FDD-Wavelet OMA: FDD gives frequencies and mode shapes, CWT of the cyclically averaged correlation functions gives damping. Works for weak (ambient) and strong (earthquake) records, short or long. Optimal Morlet parameters come from minimizing entropy. Results beat the classic methods and match exact numerical solutions.
stated_limitations_or_future_work: Validation in this paper is on numerical models. Field application was left to later work (Karun IV, Pacoima).
belongs_reason: Consensus lists R. Tarinejad as first author. Co-author Damadipour is a known collaborator. Already Consensus-verified and found again in query 1.

title: Full-scale experimental modal analysis of an arch dam: The first experience in Iran
structure_type: arch dam (Shahid Rajaee concrete arch dam, northern Iran)
methods: forced vibration test with crest-mounted exciters (in-phase / out-of-phase)
on-off and frequency-sweep tests (0.1 Hz steps)
FE model calibrated with earlier ambient tests
key_findings: First full-scale forced-vibration modal test of an arch dam in Iran. Nine middle modes and their damping ratios were estimated up to 14 Hz. Eight modes agree well with the calibrated FE model of the dam-reservoir-foundation system.
stated_limitations_or_future_work: The exciters had limited maximum force and there were too few sensors, so two sensor arrangements were needed. The lowest modes were not captured; the later B-SSI paper (2018) reanalysed the data and found them.
belongs_reason: Tarinejad is first author, with Ahmadi (Tarbiat Modares, PhD supervisor) and Harichandran (known collaborator). This matches the leads exactly.

title: Modal identification of arch dams using balanced stochastic subspace identification
structure_type: arch dam (Shahid Rajaee forced-vibration data; Pacoima Dam 2001 San Fernando earthquake records)

On Pacoima, frequencies and damping were accurate and computation time fell by up to 50%.
stated_limitations_or_future_work: Motivated by uncertainty from unknown forces, ambient noise and measurement error. Follow-up papers study uncertainty and Hankel-dimension sensitivity (Karun IV, 2022/23).

title: Damage detection based on system identification of concrete dams using an extended finite element-wavelet transform coupled procedure

title: A new approach to generating non-uniform support excitation at topographic sites

title: Soft Computing and Predicting Labyrinth Gates Discharge Coefficient
methods: Support Vector Machine (RBF, polynomial, linear, sigmoid kernels)
key_findings: Uses 345 experimental points (70% train, 30% test). The RBF-kernel SVM predicted Cd best. Adding a sill to a labyrinth sliding gate raised Cd by 9.9%, 11.8%, 13.4% and 20.8% for sill widths of 5, 15, 20 and 30.5 cm compared with a standard sliding gate.
stated_limitations_or_future_work: Not retrieved.
belongs_reason: ResearchGate listing names Abbaszadeh and Reza Tarinejad. Machine learning for hydraulic gates fits his hydraulic-structures and physical-modelling profile. One summary also mentioned a February 2026 Water Practice & Technology paper by the same pair, which a follow-up search could not confirm.

title: A Novel Complex Frequency-Domain Approach Using Power Spectral Density Transmissibility to Extract Dynamic Characteristics
structure_type: gravity dam (Koyna Dam, three excitation records)
key_findings: Reduces spectral leakage near poles and separates closely spaced modes better in short earthquake records. On noisy Koyna responses, the 4th-mode frequency error is at most 2% and damping error 5% for frequency shifts above 120. Frequency errors are under 2.5% for all modes.
stated_limitations_or_future_work: Conventional techniques give large pole errors for closely spaced modes, and short non-periodic seismic records increase spectral dispersion in higher modes. Validation is numerical (Koyna).
belongs_reason: Web-search summaries give the authors as Reza Tarinejad and Farhad Amanzad (same pair as JSV 2025). The Springer page was blocked, so the author list was not seen directly, and there was no Consensus quota left to check it.

title: Optimized Mesh Zoning for Dam Bottom Outlet CFD Simulations Using Richardson Extrapolation and Grid Convergence Analysis
key_findings: Systematic mesh-zoning based on Richardson extrapolation and GCI picks locally optimal resolutions. The zoned grid cuts total cell count by about 35-40% versus uniform refinement while keeping deviations below about 2-3% in discharge coefficient, wall pressure distribution and key flow-field parameters.
stated_limitations_or_future_work: Not retrieved (full text blocked). The model is two-dimensional, which implies 3D effects such as gate-slot flow and air entrainment are not captured.
belongs_reason: Wiley listing and search snippet give the author list Vaseti, Akhtari, Reza Tarinejad. Hydraulic-structures topic matches his listed expertise. Confirms the web lead.

title: Investigation of the Effects of Internal Structure and Material Properties on the Hydraulic Performance of Rectangular Gabion Weirs: Experimental and Numerical Study
methods: CFD (turbulence model comparison: RNG k-epsilon, standard k-epsilon, k-omega, LES)
key_findings: Studied Cd of broad-crested rectangular gabion weirs both experimentally and numerically. The RNG model matched best compared with k-epsilon, k-omega and LES. Total discharge rises with upstream head, but higher heads and more through-flow raise energy losses and lower discharge efficiency.
stated_limitations_or_future_work: Not retrieved.
belongs_reason: Reza Tarinejad (Faculty of Civil Engineering, University of Tabriz) is a co-author with Tabriz colleagues Abbaszadeh and Roushangar. Daneshfaraz (University of Maragheh) is a known collaborator. The author order is not fully certain.
